summary: Eight source-judged one-sided bounds retained; contextual anchors made explicit. No chapter/date approval.

sourceDate.text: 夜觀星象…張涼州 (s0016–s0017; following Zhang Gui’s 永甯初 appointment as 涼州刺史 in s0013)

after.event: Palace librarian who read the stars.

changes.reason: Miao Shizheng is the named participant in the night observation in s0016. The speakers call Zhang Gui 張涼州 in s0017; s0013 has just established his appointment as 涼州刺史 at 永甯初. Their assessment concerns his government after that appointment, not an ancient quoted observation. The verified Yongning start supplies onOrAfter AD 301; no exact observation year or upper endpoint is asserted. The title and appointment anchor support the lower bound beyond mere sentence adjacency.

sourceDate.text: 夜觀星象…張涼州 (s0016–s0017; following Zhang Gui’s 永甯初 appointment as 涼州刺史 in s0013)

changes.reason: Zhi Yu is the second named participant in the same night observation in s0016. The shared speech calls Zhang Gui 張涼州 in s0017, presupposing the appointment as 涼州刺史 at 永甯初 in s0013. Thus onOrAfter AD 301 is supported for Zhi Yu’s own observation; it is not Zhang Gui’s appointment mislabeled as Zhi Yu’s event. The exact observation year and upper endpoint remain unstated rather than conflicted.

sourceDate.text: 惠帝遣加 after 永興中

before.unresolvedReason: s0024 惠帝遣加 is written after the 永興中 victory but is not itself dated 永興. Yongxing opens AD 304; do not close 304–306 from the era span or from Hui's later death.
before.event: Emperor Hui added Zhang Gui as General Who Pacifies the West and marquis of Anle township after the Yongxing victory.

sourceDate.text: 惠帝遣加 (s0024, following the 永興中 victory in s0023; Emperor Hui of Western Jin)

after.event: Emperor Hui added Zhang Gui as General Who Pacifies the West and marquis of Anle township after the Yongxing victory.

changes.reason: s0023 dates Zhang Gui’s victory to 永興中; s0024 immediately reports Emperor Hui’s resulting promotion and enfeoffment, followed by 於是 in s0025. This is Hui’s own act of granting the honors, so the attestation owner p020 is correct. The contextual Yongxing start gives a conservative onOrAfter AD 304 lower bound, not an exact event year. Neither the full era span nor an imported death date is used as an upper endpoint.

sourceDate.text: 索輔言 after 湣帝即位

before.unresolvedReason: After s0122 湣帝即位 (conventional 建興元年 / AD 313). The cited Chinese writes 索輔言 / 是時 / 帝遣, not 建興元年. Do not close 313–313.

sourceDate.text: 索輔言於軌 (s0123–s0129, in the post-湣帝即位 narrative of s0122; Min’s accession conventionally AD 313)

changes.reason: s0122 introduces Emperor Min’s accession and Zhang Gui’s refusal of promotion. The ensuing s0123–s0129 is Suo Fu’s current proposal to Gui and Gui’s adoption of it: 今 in s0128 returns from historical precedents to current conditions. The 二漢 and 泰始中 inside the speech date past monetary practice, not Suo Fu’s speaking. The post-accession setting supports onOrAfter AD 313, with no claim that the speech occurred exactly in Jianxing 1 and no inferred endpoint.

sourceDate.text: 是時劉曜寇北地 (s0130; 是時 refers to the post-湣帝即位 setting introduced at s0122)

changes.reason: Liu Yao himself raids Beidi in s0130. 是時 resumes the contemporary narrative after Gui adopts Suo Fu’s proposal, in the setting introduced by Min’s accession at s0122. It does not refer back to the Han or Taishi historical examples embedded in the speech. This supports onOrAfter AD 313 for Liu Yao’s raid without identifying an exact Jianxing year or inventing an upper bound.

changes.reason: Qu Tao’s own attested role is leading the force sent to defend Chang’an in response to Liu Yao’s raid in s0130. 是時 explicitly links this contemporary action to the narrative after Min’s accession in s0122, not the antiquarian chronology within Suo Fu’s quotation. The onOrAfter AD 313 bound preserves only the established accession floor; no exact dispatch year or upper endpoint is inferred.

after.event: Grand herald sent to honor Zhang Gui.

changes.reason: Xin Pan is the envoy in s0131; the emperor sending him continues Emperor Min named in s0122. Gui again refuses (又固辭), echoing the refusal after Min’s accession. This identifies both the event owner and the reigning emperor. An act of this emperor belongs onOrAfter his verified AD 313 accession; no exact Jianxing year or endpoint is introduced.

before.unresolvedReason: s0007 泰始初 is an era-opening label, not a closed Gregorian year. Conventional Taishi 1 = AD 265 as a reign-year label; the era opened in the last lunar month of 265 (十二月丙寅 is already AD 266 Gregorian), so this is not a December/January day date.
before.event: At the beginning of Taishi, Zhang Gui received fifth-rank office through his uncle Zhang Xi.

sourceDate.text: 泰始初 (Jin Wu’s Taishi opening period; conventional era-start label AD 265, not an exact Gregorian event year)

after.event: At the beginning of Taishi, Zhang Gui received fifth-rank office through his uncle Zhang Xi.

changes.reason: s0007 explicitly places Zhang Gui’s fifth-rank appointment through his uncle Zhang Xi in 泰始初. This is Jin Wu’s Taishi in his early career, not the Taishi cited retrospectively in Suo Fu’s speech. AD 265 is the conventional era-start year and a conservative on-or-after bound, even though the opening day is in Gregorian AD 266. 初 supplies no exact event year or upper endpoint; that lack of precision is fully represented by the one-sided bound and is not a remaining conversion or ownership conflict.
